newsitem.title: USA: G7 praises progress made by some African nations.
newsitem.headline: G7 praises progress made by some African nations.

text.p: The Group of Seven on Sunday praised the progress that some African nations are making on the economic front and expressed its determination to support those reforms.

"We are greatly encouraged by the strong performance of certain sub-Saharan countries," the G7 said in a statement issued after five hours of talks. "We are determined to support these reforms as effectively as possible."
Such steps would include granting enhanced debt relief to poor countries and giving their exports greater access to industrial countries' markets.

The International Monetary Fund and World Bank last week put in practise a long-awaited aid initiative for poor countries by granting debt relief to Uganda. The Paris Club of creditor nations has also agreed to join in.
"We look forward to timely decisions on additional countries," the group said.
In its statement, the G7 -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- also urged other creditors to participate in the multi-billion-dollar program as soon as possible.
Noting that bribery and corruption have "corrosive effects" on economic development, the G7 called for further action to combat those illegal practises.

It urged the IMF and World Bank to expand their efforts to help developing countries to fight corruption. It also called on industrial nations to make foreign bribery a crime and to quickly eliminate any tax breaks for such bribes.

The group also welcomed the progress that had been made by the IMF's executive board on increasing the monetary fund's resources and agreed that it was important for the lending agencies to have adequate resources.
But the statement made no mention of how much of an increase in the IMF's resources might be needed.
At their meeting, the G7 nations also reviewed progress made on promoting financial stability in emerging markets.

The 11-nation Group of Ten -- which includes the G7 plus Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden and Switzerland -- is expected to release a report this week detailing steps aimed at reducing the risk of financial crises in such markets.

The strategy includes agreement on a set of core guidelines and principles as well as specific recommendations for international financial institutions and regulators on how to help emerging market economies implement them.
In its communique, the G7 endorsed the strategy and suggested that regulators and others work together to implement it.
